newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on strong dollar.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Wednesday, as the dollar's gains against the yen encouraged individual investors to buy, traders said.
Prices were 60 to 190 yen higher, with the benchmark November 1997 up 190 at 14,140 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 45,058 lots.

Nearby months were weaker at the opening, reflecting the bearish mood of the CBOT market overnight. The dollar firmed later due to relief at the results of the U.S. election. Television projections showed the Republicans likely to take both houses of Congress -- a best-case scenario for the dollar.
The dollar's gains against the yen triggered active buying in the afternoon, traders said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A corn trading system was being traded at $2.59-1/2 per bushel at 0800 GMT, against $2.58-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
The spot November of the CBOT soybean futures on the Project A overnight trading system was at $6.73-1/4 at 0800 GMT, against $6.70 at Tuesday's close.
